questions.template: Marcus scored VII in the arena. What number is VII?
questions.hint: V is 5, and each I adds one more.
questions.explain: VII = V (5) + I + I (2) = 7. Read left to right, adding as you go.

questions.hint: A small I BEFORE the X means one LESS than ten.
questions.explain: IX = 10 − 1 = 9. When a smaller numeral comes first, subtract it!

questions.template: The arena clock shows XII. What hour is that?
questions.hint: X is ten, and II adds two more.
questions.explain: XII = X (10) + II (2) = 12 — the top of every clock in Rome!

questions.hint: I before V takes one away from five.
questions.explain: IV = 5 − 1 = 4. Romans loved this subtraction shortcut.

questions.hint: Ten, then four: X then IV.

questions.template: The scoreboard shows XVI. What's the score?
questions.explain: XVI = 10 + 5 + 1 = 16. Add left to right when big comes first.

questions.hint: L is 50 — and the X before it takes ten AWAY.
questions.explain: XL = 50 − 10 = 40. Small before big means subtract.

questions.template: A legion has LXXV soldiers. How many is that?
questions.explain: LXXV = 50 + 10 + 10 + 5 = 75. March through it numeral by numeral!

questions.hint: C is 100. X before C subtracts ten.
questions.explain: XC = 100 − 10 = 90. The subtraction trick works for tens too.
99 = 90 + 9 = XC + IX = XCIX. Never subtract more than one step!
